title: 2027 State Minimum Wage Increases Impacting Manufacturers
summary: Minimum wages are set to rise in 16 states on January 1. See how the increases hit plant labor costs, wage steps, and merit budgets—and plan for 2027.
body_markdown:
For manufacturers operating plants in multiple states, there's no single minimum wage to plan for in 2027. Sixteen states will raise their minimum wages on January 1, with increases ranging from under 2% to over 9%.


Most increases fall between 3% and 4%, though Michigan, Virginia, and Rhode Island are significantly higher, while Nebraska is much lower. These differences will affect your labor budget at each plant, so address them before year-end.


## State-by-state increases for 2027


Fifteen rates are confirmed; Vermont’s rate is inflation-based and will be announced in the first week of January.
‍


New York is a notable exception: its standard wage remains $17.00 in NYC, Long Island, and Westchester, and $16.00 elsewhere. Missouri is also unchanged. Monitor a[New York proposal](https://www.governor.ny.gov/new-york-state-minimum-wage-2027) that could alter these rates on March 1, 2027.


## How the floor compares with 2027 raise budgets


Pave and Alpine Rewards teamed up to release the[2027 Compensation Budgets & Planning Report](https://explore.pave.com/2027-budgets-trends-report.html) , which showed the median U.S. merit budget at 3.5% of payroll. Ten of the sixteen state increases meet or exceed this figure, with Washington matching it. Vermont’s projected 3.4% is slightly below.


For plant teams, entry wages in these states are increasing faster than typical raises for current employees. Operators just above the minimum may see new hires quickly close the pay gap, even after a standard[merit increase](https://www.pave.com/blog-posts/merit-budgets-2027) . Remember, 3.5% is a median budget, not a guaranteed raise; 87% of surveyed companies link merit increases to individual performance ratings.
‍


Two additional findings are relevant. Surveyed companies report promotional increases averaging 9% to 12%, roughly three times a typical merit raise, making promotions a clear way to restore pay separation. Additionally, 80% of companies post pay ranges in all U.S. job listings, so candidates and staff will see new entry rates. With 60% expecting to add headcount in 2027,[hiring competition may increase](https://www.pave.com/blog-posts/pricing-manufacturing-roles) .


## Where labor cost shows up beyond the entry rate


The increase affects your lowest-paid roles first, but the budget impact extends further. As entry rates rise, operators, material handlers, and leads just above them often require adjustments as well, so total costs typically exceed the headline percentage applied to minimum-wage payroll. The table lists the areas to review at each site.
‍


Since the impact varies by plant, review the table for each site individually rather than for the company as a whole.


## A Q4 checklist for plant and HR leaders


1. Map every plant to its state and local minimum wage, and note which states change on January 1.
2. Re-run the 2027 labor budget for each plant using that plant's actual increase, not a company average.
3. List roles paid within about a dollar of the new minimum and decide which rates should move.
4. Compare merit and promotion plans for those roles with the size of the floor increase.
5. Review overtime and shift-premium formulas, agency agreements, and any union or internal wage scales tied to entry pay.
6. Test location, sourcing, and automation assumptions against the state-by-state differences.
7. Update payroll, posted notices, and manager talking points before the first January paycheck.


## Check back in January


Vermont’s rate is inflation-based and will be announced in the first week of January. The table uses a projected rate of approximately $14.91; update this once the state confirms the final rate.


New York’s standard wage is currently frozen, but the Legislature could approve a proposal to raise it on March 1, 2027, to $17.60 in NYC, Long Island, and Westchester, and $16.55 elsewhere. Home care aides will receive an increase on January 1.


City and county minimum wages may change on different dates than state rates, so verify each plant’s local rate separately.


## Bottom line for manufacturing


Most 2027 increases are modest but not uniform, and the resulting costs also vary. Managing each plant’s labor budget individually, reviewing pay levels above the entry rate, and aligning merit plans with minimum wage changes will prepare you for January’s open items.
